# Converted from Slurm directives.

# Flux resource request equivalents:
# --nodes=1, --ntasks-per-node=1  => 1 task (rank) on 1 node

conda deactivate
conda activate new

module load python

# Execute the python script
# Slurm used: srun python nas.py
# Flux equivalent: run under Flux as a 1-rank task
flux run -n 1 -c 8 -g 1 python nas.py

EOF
"

#!/bin/bash

# Flux batch script
# Converted from Slurm directives.

# Flux resource request equivalents:
# --nodes=1, --ntasks-per-node=1  => 1 task (rank) on 1 node
# --cpus-per-task=8               => 8 cores for the single task
# --gres=gpu:1                    => 1 GPU
# --time=23:59:59                 => time limit
flux batch -N 1 -n 1 -c 8 -g 1 -t 23h59m59s -o output=nas5.out <<'EOF'

# NOTE: Slurm --job-name=nas not translated.
# Performance/ops implication: the job will have a default Flux job name/description,
# which can make it harder to identify in queue/history, but does not affect runtime performance.

# NOTE: Slurm --partition=gpu not translated.
# Performance implication: without an explicit Flux queue/constraint mapping, the job may land on
# resources that satisfy the GPU request if available, but you are not forcing a specific partition/queue.

source ~/.bashrc
conda deactivate
conda activate new

# Load the python interpreter
module load python

# Execute the python script
# Slurm used: srun python nas.py
# Flux equivalent: run under Flux as a 1-rank task
flux run -n 1 -c 8 -g 1 python nas.py

EOF

reasons: Uses `flux batch` inside a script without any `#flux`/`#SBATCH`-style resource directives; as a batch script submitted to Flux (e.g., `flux batch script.sh`), Flux will ignore the embedded `flux batch ...` line for resource allocation and instead allocate default resources, so the requested nodes/cores/gpus/time/output are not actually applied to the submitted job.

The resource request is expressed as CLI flags to an inner `flux batch` command, which only takes effect if this script is executed in an existing Flux instance; that is not a valid way to declare resources for the outer job submission itself.

The `-g 1` GPU request may not be accepted on some Flux installations unless the resource model is configured with generic resources (G) and the `-g` option is enabled; portability of this resource directive is not guaranteed.
issues: If you submit this file with `flux batch script.sh`, it will start a job that then submits a second nested job via `flux batch ... <<EOF`, which is typically unintended and can fail if the inner job cannot connect to the broker (or can lead to double-scheduling).

To make it a proper Flux batch script, you typically either (a) submit via CLI: `flux batch -N 1 -n 1 -c 8 -g 1 -t 23h59m59s -o output=nas5.out script.sh` and remove the heredoc, or (b) use Flux batch directives supported by your site (if available) rather than nesting `flux batch`.
